howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Type a keyword (heart, party, cry) to search emojis, symbols and kaomoji at once. Korean keywords work too
Tap an item to copy it. To build a string, switch to 'Collect', tap several items, then press 'Copy all'
Pick a skin tone and person/hand emojis are copied in that tone
The Symbols tab is grouped like the Korean IME consonant + Hanja key lists
The 'Selected' panel shows the Unicode code points and HTML entity with copy buttons

tips.title: Tips
items: Recently used items stay at the top so you do not need to search for the same emoji again
If you type Korean with the keyboard still set to English, such as gkxm, the search converts it to the intended Korean word
Share a link with ?q=heart to open the same search
Emoji designs differ by OS and device; older devices may show an empty box (□)

whatIs.title: What is the Emoji Picker?
whatIs.description: Find about 650 popular emojis, symbols (★ ♥ → ① ℃ ㎡ ₩) and kaomoji (¯\_(ツ)_/¯) in one place and copy them with a single tap. Includes skin tones, a collect-and-copy tray, and Unicode/HTML codes for each character.

items.q: Can I search in both Korean and English?
items.a: Yes. Korean ('하트'), English ('heart') and Korean initial consonants ('ㅎㅌ') all work. You can also paste an emoji to see its code points.

items.q: Why do some copied emojis look different or broken in other apps?
items.a: Emojis follow the Unicode standard, but Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft draw them differently. If the receiving OS or app does not support an emoji, it may show an empty box (□) or a separate skin-tone swatch.

items.q: How do I type symbols from the keyboard?
items.a: On Windows with the Korean IME, type a consonant (ㅁ, ㅇ, ㄴ…) and press the Hanja key to get a symbol list: ㅁ for shapes (★♥※), ㅇ for circled characters (①㉠), ㄹ for units (℃㎡₩), ㄴ for brackets (「」【】).
